body:
hey there -

You no longer need to use a TypeDecorator for the UUID like that, in 2.0 you can use the [Uuid](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/type_basics.html#sqlalchemy.types.Uuid) datatype that will do all the SQL Server UNIQUEIDENTIFIER and all of that.

otherwise, in order to be compatible with [insertmanyvalues](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/connections.html#engine-insertmanyvalues), your type must implement a new method [_sentinel_value_resolver](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/e3f7bc683ac3ea6d7c517b9c7ffeaa911860d732/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/type_api.py#L577) if it is going to be a. used as a primary key / autoincrementing type and b. sends off bound parameters to an INSERT statement in a different form than they would be coming back from a RETURNING by the driver, in this case strings go in and UUIDs come out.   This method was introduced in 2.0.10 to suit a major issue that was discovered in insertmanyvalues which is discussed [here](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/changelog/changelog_20.html#change-d31d59ce83faf9c31b77aa69d2838bd4) and [here](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/connections.html#engine-insertmanyvalues-returning-order).

this method obviously should not remain as an underscored method, it should become something public and part of whats mentioned in the insertmanyvalues section as well as in a note for `TypeDecorator`.

for your type to work on PostgreSQL the method can be written as:

```py

class GUID(TypeDecorator):
    """Platform-independent GUID type.

    Uses PostgreSQL's UUID type or MSSQL's UNIQUEIDENTIFIER,
    otherwise uses CHAR(32), storing as stringified hex values.

    """

    impl = CHAR
    cache_ok = True

    _default_type = CHAR(32)
    _uuid_as_str = attrgetter("hex")

    def _sentinel_value_resolver(self, dialect):
        """For the "insertmanyvalues" feature only, return a callable that
        will receive the uuid object or string
        as it is normally passed to the DB in the parameter set, after
        bind_processor() is called.  Convert this value to match
        what it would be as coming back from a RETURNING or similar
        statement for the given backend.

        Individual dialects and drivers may need their own implementations
        based on how their UUID types send data and how the drivers behave
        (e.g. pyodbc)

        """

        # PG / MSSQL dialects, we sent strings, but we get back uuids.
        # need to convert them
        if dialect.name in ("postgresql", "mssql"):
            return uuid.UUID
        else:
            # otherwise, seems like we would have passed UUID values?
            return None

# .. rest of type
```

rename.from: Postgres insertmany - Can't match sentinel values in result set to parameter sets
rename.to: document _sentinel_value_resolver for custom TypeDecorator classes, include note in types / insertmanyvalues.  likely make a public method

body: Thanks for the quick response. Like I mentioned, I'm using SQLModel which implements the GUID class [here](https://github.com/tiangolo/sqlmodel/blob/4c3f242ae215b28ef7b1dcb37411531999826d0d/sqlmodel/sql/sqltypes.py#L24) in order to create a UUID data type. If this is expected behavior then I can open the issue there, and point them to your comment above.

it would be easier if they used our `Uuid` type which supersedes the older GUID TypeDecorator.   The `_sentinel_value_resolver` is a new method that had to be introduced mid-stream and we havent really picked a public API for it yet, and the underscored name will change to something non-underscored.   I might add a simpler method to TypeDecorator also.    so if they do "_sentinel_value_resolver" that might have to change later

rename.from: document _sentinel_value_resolver for custom TypeDecorator classes, include note in types / insertmanyvalues.  likely make a public method
rename.to: make public version of _sentinel_value_resolver and document, *OR* rework sentinel logic to use pre-bindparam types + result procsesed

body: there might also be a way for me to rework this code, with some complexity, to work differently and not really need this method.  but it might be less efficient in some cases.
Created a discussion [here](https://github.com/tiangolo/sqlmodel/discussions/843#discussion-6376204) showing the SQLModel version, and linking back to this issue. Thanks for your help.

I think this issue will be solved of you don't stringify the uuid.
Try doing
```py
elif dialect.name in ("postgresql", "mssql"):
     return value
```

> I think this issue will be solved of you don't stringify the uuid. Try doing
> 
> ```python
> elif dialect.name in ("postgresql", "mssql"):
>      return value
> ```

This fixes my issue in the code above, but that code is taken from the SQLAlchemy [docs](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/custom_types.html#backend-agnostic-guid-type). And SQLModel would have to update their GUID class [here](https://github.com/tiangolo/sqlmodel/blob/4c3f242ae215b28ef7b1dcb37411531999826d0d/sqlmodel/sql/sqltypes.py#L45).  Is that the proper fix?
well it's a fix, the sqlalchemy docs should probably be updated to avoid converting uuid to strings

I'd rather make this method obsolete, this nuance is too hard to explain going forward and is unnecessary.  I was going to try to rework insertmanyvalues to work with the pre-bound original value and compare against the result value which would be run through result processor.

Not 100% this would solve this use case though.
Like I believe some options of Uuid would break that use case, like `as_uuid=False, native_uuild=True` where the user passes in uuid. 

Overall this almost seems like the best option could be to just not use uuid for this

the data sent in for UUID and the data coming out must match.    it wouldn't work to send in a string and get back a UUID, I think the ORM itself already will have problems with that re: the identity map.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**remove sentinel_value_resolvers and use pre-bind values** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/5208

if a user was using as_uuid=False I think they are required to pass a string as the datatype.   Also, if they are hand-populating UUIDs in their objects, then the sentinel is not needed for that value anyway; this only deals with Python-side default generators.    if people get this error because they are using `uuid.uuid4` as their default generator and they have as_uuid=False, we just tell them to make sure the default is `lambda: str(uuid.uuid4())` or whatever, that's easier to document, easier to explain, and they dont need SQLModel to make fixes

# What

Update SQLAlchemy to address the bulk insert failure shown [here](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/11160).

# Why

Bulk inserts are now working again.
